note: Generated by scripts/map.mjs. Machine-readable reload for agents; see PROJECT_MAP.md for prose.

project.name: brewdocs
project.tagline: Brew your docs, serve them hot.
project.what:
A zero-config documentation generator for code. Point it at a local path, an npm package name, or a GitHub URL and it produces one self-contained HTML page (plus a queryable `docmodel.json`). It also ships a hosting server, a CLI with coverage/diff/gate tooling, language adapters beyond JS/TS, and an MCP server so agents can read the same model.

The product's whole job is rendering prose from repositories **you do not own** — READMEs, doc comments, git tag names. That is the threat model everything in `facts/invariants.json` follows from.
project.audience: Maintainers of the monorepo and anyone hosting `brewdocs serve` on a reachable address.

invariants.rule: The hosting server binds 127.0.0.1 unless the operator passes --host. A non-loopback bind with no token and no keys mints a token before serving.
invariants.why: `server.listen(port)` binds every interface on Node. The build API can run npm install, so an open instance on a LAN is remote code execution, and the startup banner used to say 'localhost' while the socket said otherwise.

invariants.rule: Fetching an npm package must pass --ignore-scripts and must not pass the parent process environment through to the child.
invariants.why: BrewDocs only needs a package's README and source to build docs. Lifecycle scripts (postinstall et al.) are arbitrary code execution from a caller-supplied name, reachable from the build API.

invariants.rule: Every endpoint that reads a caller-supplied local path must resolve it against sourceRoot and refuse anything outside with 403. Realpath first, so neither .. nor a symlink escapes.
invariants.why: A build endpoint that renders any readable directory is a file-disclosure primitive; /api/export returned the HTML directly, so a README containing a key was disclosed verbatim.

invariants.rule: HTML escaping has one implementation (packages/core/src/escape.ts) that escapes " and ' as well as & < >, because untrusted values are interpolated into quoted attributes (href, value, title).
invariants.why: This is the contract, not one call site. The XSS shipped because escapeHtml escaped only &<>; local copies then multiplied (highlight, workspaces, registry, federation) and the gate only checked three fixed files. One source plus an all-files scan keeps a new quote-blind helper from slipping in.
invariants.enforcedBy: packages/core/src/escape.ts (the single escaper) + scripts/gate.mjs (inv-4:escape-helpers-quote-safe scans every source file) + packages/core/test/escape.test.ts

invariants.rule: Path containment must be boundary-aware: resolve the candidate and require it to equal the root or start with root + path.sep. Never use a bare startsWith.
invariants.why: startsWith accepted a sibling whose name shared the target's prefix (/s/acme/../acme-secret resolved outside hosting/acme). The existing traversal test passed for the wrong reason — Node's URL normalizer, not the code.

invariants.rule: A site subdomain must be a plain DNS-ish slug; dots-only and separator-bearing values are refused before any path resolution.
invariants.why: The Host header is caller-controlled and `...brewdocs.dev` slugifies to `..`, which reaches above the hosting directory.

invariants.rule: A URL placed in href/src must have its scheme validated; javascript:, vbscript: and data: are dropped, including control-character-smuggled forms.
invariants.why: Markdown link targets come from third-party prose. `java\nscript:` is still javascript: to a browser, so the scheme check must strip control characters before sniffing.

invariants.rule: Any writer that takes a site-root-relative path from config must resolve it against the output directory and refuse anything outside. Same boundary-aware rule as INV-5: no bare startsWith.
invariants.why: `redirects:` and `aliases:` in brewdocs.yml are repo-controlled, so a `from: "../x.html"` key could create files above the build output. Reachable from any repo you build docs for.

invariants.rule: A theme slot partial path must be confined to the manifest's source root before it is read.
invariants.why: Slot values are repo-controlled config. A `themes/brand.yml` shipped by the repo being documented could name `../../id_rsa`; the build would read it and can embed it in a page the user then publishes.
invariants.enforcedBy: packages/plugin-sdk/test/v2.test.ts (confines slot partials to the source root)

invariants.rule: A POST (write) request must be refused with 403 when the browser signals a cross-site origin: Origin must equal the Host we were reached on, and Sec-Fetch-Site must be same-origin or none.
invariants.why: Any web page can POST to an open instance on the user's LAN with a simple request and no preflight. Non-browser clients send neither header and stay allowed.

invariants.rule: CI workflows must install with npm ci, never npm install.
invariants.why: A lockfile-ignoring install on a tree containing package.json scripts is a supply-chain surface; the Pages workflow ran on a repository with pages: write and id-token: write granted.

invariants.rule: The published @brewdocs/core must resolve to compiled JS (dist/), not raw TypeScript, so a plain-Node consumer can import it.
invariants.why: Core shipped src/**/*.ts; `import '@brewdocs/core'` under plain Node threw ERR_UNSUPPORTED_NODE_MODULES_TYPE_STRIPPING. Dev/test keep using source via tsconfig paths + a vitest alias, so only the published entry changes.

invariants.rule: A per-user API key must only perform the operations its scopes include; a write endpoint with the wrong scope returns 403.
invariants.why: keys.ts stored and printed scopes that server.ts never read, so a `--scope build` key could export and render markdown too. The surface advertised a boundary it did not have.
invariants.enforcedBy: packages/cli/src/server.test.ts (enforces the key's scopes per write endpoint)

invariants.rule: A release tag must run the verify gate (typecheck + map + security invariants + tests) before publishing.
invariants.why: publish.yml published three packages on any v* tag after only `npm ci` + `npm test`; provenance attests where it was built, not that it works.

invariants.rule: X-Forwarded-For may only set the rate-limit client identity behind an explicit opt-in (trustProxy / BREWDOCS_TRUST_PROXY=1); otherwise the socket address is used.
invariants.why: The header is caller-controlled, so honouring it unconditionally let a client defeat the only brake on the expensive /api/build path by rotating the value.

invariants.rule: Read endpoints that expose deployment/registry/federation metadata must 401 once auth is configured (admin token or keys); only a fully unauthenticated instance leaves them open.
invariants.why: needsAuth was driven by the token alone, so an instance with keys but no BREWDOCS_TOKEN leaked /api/sites, /api/registry, /api/search and the stats rollup anonymously.
invariants.enforcedBy: scripts/gate.mjs (inv-16:read-endpoints-guarded) + packages/cli/src/server.test.ts (guards read endpoints once auth is configured)

invariants.rule: An adapter that executes code against the source tree (python) must refuse a fetched (npm/git) source and run only for a locally chosen one.
invariants.why: The python adapter shells out to a bundled AST helper; running it against a package the user did not choose turns a doc build into code execution on attacker-supplied input.

invariants.rule: The renderer must have a golden-output snapshot test over a full page, including hostile inputs.
invariants.why: A renderer that emits its own CSS/JS had no output test, which is how the attribute-injection XSS (#3) survived hundreds of green unit tests that only checked substrings.

invariants.rule: Every write endpoint (POST) must carry an explicit guard (authorize / guardSource / requireSiteAccess) before it acts on caller input.
invariants.why: The build/export/markdown APIs are the RCE and file-disclosure surface. A new POST route added without a guard would ship open; the gate asserts the guard from the routes it parses out of server.ts.

invariants.rule: A fetched (npm/git) source must not be able to name its own plugins: plugins listed in the source's brewdocs.yml are ignored unless the source was chosen locally. Plugins the operator passed explicitly (--plugins) still load.
invariants.why: A plugin is arbitrary code — loaded via require/import, with no signature and no sandbox. The specifier is read from the source's own brewdocs.yml, and BrewDocs' stated job is rendering repos you do not own, so honoring it turns every doc build into remote code execution on the operator's machine. This is the same threat INV-17 already refuses for the python adapter, in a wider blast radius. The subtle part is propagation:  must survive every hop from resolveInput to resolveSetup, and each hop that rebuilt a Source without it silently re-enabled the repo's plugins. That is how the first version of this fix was bypassed three times (per-version worktree, extractVersion, and the CLI build command) before the gate check was written to assert all of them.
invariants.enforcedBy: packages/core/test/plugin-fetched.test.ts + scripts/gate.mjs (inv-20:fetched-source-cannot-name-plugins, which asserts the guard and every Source re-construction site)

findings.title: serve bound every interface with auth off (RCE via npm postinstall)
Unauthenticated build API rendered any absolute local path
Attribute injection / XSS: escapeHtml did not escape quotes
Subdomain `..` escaped the hosting dir; CLI --name was never slugified
findings.detail: Server-side slug guard landed in v3.7.0 (checkedBy inv-6). The CLI deploy path now always routes the requested name through combineSubdomain, so `brewdocs deploy --name ../x` slugifies to `x` instead of writing outside the hosting dir.

findings.title: emitRedirects wrote outside outDir via a `from: "../x"` key
findings.detail: Reachable from any repo's brewdocs.yml (`redirects:`). The `skip: file exists` guard prevented overwriting but not creating outside the output tree. emitAliasPages was checked at the same time: its alias name goes through dirSafe, which maps separators to `_`, so it could not traverse â€” but the write target is now confirmed inside outDir anyway.

findings.title: publish.yml publishes on any v* tag with no typecheck or smoke build
findings.detail: publish.yml ran only `npm ci` + `npm test`, so a tag on a commit whose types do not compile still published three packages. It now runs `npm run verify` (typecheck + map + gate + tests) plus a smoke build before any publish. Provenance attests where it was built, not that it works.

findings.title: @brewdocs/core ships raw TypeScript; plain Node cannot import it
findings.detail: Core shipped raw src/**/*.ts, so `import '@brewdocs/core'` under plain Node threw ERR_UNSUPPORTED_NODE_MODULES_TYPE_STRIPPING. It now builds to dist (tsconfig.build.json, excluding tests), ships dist/ with a types+import exports map, and builds via prepublishOnly. Dev, tests and typecheck still resolve workspace source through tsconfig paths + a vitest alias, so the CLI keeps running TS directly (D-2).

findings.title: API key scopes are stored and printed but never enforced
findings.detail: keys.ts persisted and printed `scopes` but server.ts never read them, so a `--scope build` key performed every operation. Write endpoints now call authorize(req, scope) and return 403 when the key's scopes do not include build/export/markdown; the admin token still grants all, and a key with no scopes means all (keys.ts).

findings.title: Rate limiter trusts X-Forwarded-For unconditionally
findings.detail: clientKey() trusted X-Forwarded-For unconditionally, so rotating the header defeated the limiter. It now keys on the socket address unless the operator opts in via ProtectionOptions.trustProxy / BREWDOCS_TRUST_PROXY=1.

findings.title: Analytics/registry endpoints leak when keys exist but no admin token is set
findings.detail: needsAuth was driven by the token, so with keys present and BREWDOCS_TOKEN unset, /api/sites, /api/registry, /api/search and the /api/stats rollup answered unauthenticated. They now call authorizeRead and 401 unless the admin token or a valid key is presented; with no auth configured at all they stay open for the local drop-in UI.

findings.title: Theme slot partials resolved relative to the manifest (arbitrary file read)
findings.detail: A themes/brand.yml committed by a repo owner could name a slot value like ../../id_rsa; manifestSlots() read it and the build could embed it in a published page. Slot partials are now confined to the manifest's source root (recorded by loadThemeManifest as `sourceRoot`), boundary-aware in the same way as INV-5.

findings.title: Pages workflow uses npm install instead of npm ci
findings.detail: .github/workflows/brewdocs.yml ran `npm install` on a tree that contains package.json scripts, with pages: write + id-token: write granted. It now uses `npm ci`; the gate refuses any workflow that reintroduces `npm install`.

findings.title: Doc/reality drift (test counts, root package version, gitignored roadmap)
findings.detail: Test counts, file/LOC totals and the HTTP surface table are now parsed by scripts/map.mjs instead of typed, and CI fails when the map is stale. The root package.json version now tracks the three workspaces (4.1.0). ROADMAP.md remains gitignored by design (it is local planning, like AGENTS.md and the release notes).

findings.title: python adapter executes a bundled helper against the target tree
findings.detail: The python adapter executes a bundled AST helper against the tree. Sources fetched from npm/git are now flagged Source.fetched, propagated to AdapterContext, and the adapter refuses (warn + skip) rather than running against code the user did not choose locally.

findings.title: No CSRF/Origin check on write endpoints
findings.detail: Any web page could POST to an open instance on the user's LAN with a simple request (no preflight). POST endpoints now 403 when Origin does not match the Host, or Sec-Fetch-Site is not same-origin/none. Non-browser clients send neither header and are unaffected.

findings.title: No golden-output test for the renderer
findings.detail: The renderer emits its own CSS/JS and had no golden-output test, which is how the attribute-injection XSS (#3) survived 311 green tests. render.golden.test.ts now snapshots a full deterministic page with a hostile link/description, so an escaping regression fails loudly.

findings.title: api.test.ts was flaky under load (2 tests at a 30s timeout)
findings.detail: A full-suite run on 2026-09-26 failed two endpoint tests at 31.2s / 33.9s against `{ timeout: 30_000 }`; a solo run of the file passed in 28.7s and an immediate re-run of the full suite went green. Both tests do a full TS extraction synchronously, so they are sensitive to load. Found by running the suite while building the map generator.

findings.title: A fetched repo brewdocs.yml could name a plugin, executing arbitrary code at build time (RCE)
findings.detail: Reproduced by execution on 2026-09-28, not inferred: a synthetic repo whose brewdocs.yml contained plugins: [./pwn.cjs], with the plugin writing a marker file, ran that code during brewdocs build. loadPlugin resolves the specifier with requireFrom(root)(abs) — no signature, no sandbox — and build.ts called loadPlugins(config.plugins, ...) with no check of source.fetched. The guard for this class already existed and was simply not applied: finding #15 / INV-17 made the python adapter refuse a fetched source for exactly this reason. Three further bypasses were found while fixing it, all the same root cause (a Source rebuilt without carrying fetched): the per-version worktree in buildVersions, the extractVersion checkout, and the CLI build command resolveCliSource, which dropped the flag on the main brewdocs build path. All four sites now propagate fetched and resolveSetup drops repo-config plugins for a fetched source. Operator-passed --plugins still load, since that is the caller own choice, and a locally chosen source is unaffected.
